title: Tri Pointe Homes Celebrates 15 Years of Building Successful Communities in the Bay Area
content:
Since launching in 2010, the Bay Area division has developed 48 communities and closed more than 4,000 homes across 21 cities—and counting.The Bay Area division consistently delivers high-quality construction and outstanding customer service.Today, Tri Pointe Homes’ Bay Area division offers 12 unique communities, each designed to accommodate the needs of today’s homebuyers. Pictured: The Tides at River Islands in Lathrop.

SAN RAMON, Calif., April 23, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Tri Pointe Homes, Inc. (NYSE: TPH), one of the nation’s largest homebuilders, proudly marks the 15th anniversary of its Bay Area division, celebrating a decade and a half of building thoughtfully designed homes and vibrant communities across the region.

Since launching in 2010, the Bay Area division has developed 48 communities and closed more than 4,000 homes across 21 cities—and counting. Beyond these milestones, the division has remained focused on creating housing opportunities for a wide range of buyers, including first-time, move-up, and luxury homeowners.

Success was never guaranteed: As the country and region continued to recover from the global financial crisis of 2007-2009, the year 2010 was particularly challenging for the Bay Area in numerous ways. Unemployment measured by the Bureau of Labor Statistics was reaching as high as 10% to 11%, well more than double today’s rates closer to 4.0%. Median home sales prices tracked by Zillow had fallen over 25% from their 2006 peaks, while building permits reported to the Census Bureau plummeted nearly 60% from 2005’s levels.

For Tri Pointe Homes, however, it was precisely these historically challenging market conditions of 2010 into which the newly formed division focused on Northern California would excel, while also playing a pivotal role in shaping the division’s disciplined, strategic approach—one that continues to differentiate Tri Pointe from other homebuilders in the Bay Area today.

"Most builders were faced with difficult conditions and under-performing communities and financials, which allowed us to enter the market with a fresh ledger, a longer-term outlook, and more optimism and confidence," said Division President for Tri Pointe Homes Jeff Frankel. "There are still foundational lessons learned from those early days that guide us today."

Some of those most critical lessons stemmed from hurdles many developers were facing when seeking approvals for new housing projects, frequently leading to architectural and design compromises. To avoid this outcome, Frankel’s team focused on embracing relationships with city officials and intentionally taking the extra time and energy to offer more inspired community and architectural solutions while ensuring an elevated experience for homebuyers. As Frankel notes, it was precisely this team-centric culture and shared goals on providing a premium experience which translated so well to meeting the needs of the community.

Indeed, success in a highly complex housing market like the Bay Area demands regional expertise supported by a stable, high-performing team. With the Bureau of Labor Statistics reporting construction industry turnover rates which are frequently significantly higher than overall averages, retaining skilled employees is a critical priority. Fortunately, much of the Tri Pointe Homes Bay Area team has been there since the division’s start.

Story Continues

"It is a pretty simple strategy—hire good people, treat people the way you want to be treated, and get everyone aligned to our goals," said Frankel. "We always push each other to get the best results possible for the company and our customer."

As a result, both the division and company have earned prestigious workplace recognitions such as Best Places to Work in the Bay Area, Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® and Great Place to Work® certifications multiple years in a row. In addition, the Bay Area division has received multiple home design and staff accolades from the Bay Area Building Industry Association and the National Association of Home Builders.

This internal strength directly carries through to the field, where the Bay Area division consistently delivers high-quality construction and outstanding customer service. Eliant, the homebuilding industry’s leading customer experience management and insights firm, has recognized the Bay Area as the #1 Tri Pointe Homes division for homebuyer referrals in addition to multiple awards for customers’ experiences with their purchases, construction, customer service and build quality.

Today, Tri Pointe Homes’ Bay Area division offers 12 unique communities, each designed to accommodate the needs of today’s homebuyers. Actively selling neighborhoods include Swirl, Glisten, and Splash at One Lake in Fairfield; Chantara and The Tides at River Islands in Lathrop; Cascade in Vallejo; Lotus at UrbanOak in San Jose; Willow Landing in Hollister The Knolls at Mountain House in Mountain House. Priority lists are now forming for upcoming communities, including Harmony in Pleasanton, as well as Trails and Brooks at Creekside in Antioch.

Looking ahead, despite whatever challenges emerge, the division remains committed to building quality homes and communities in a region that often struggles to provide suitable new housing.

"The market is challenging right now, but who doesn’t like a good challenge?" said Frankel. "Factors including growth of the regional economy, value proposition trends and homebuyer preference have and will continue to evolve in the Bay Area. We are committed to serving the Bay Area’s need for housing solutions in a positive way over the coming years."

About Tri Pointe Homes® [Bay Area]

One of the largest homebuilders in the U.S., Tri Pointe Homes, Inc. (NYSE: TPH) is a publicly traded company operating in 12 states and the District of Columbia, and is a recognized leader in customer experience, innovative design, and environmentally responsible business practices. The company builds premium homes and communities with deep ties to the communities it serves—some for as long as a century. Tri Pointe Homes combines the financial resources, technology platforms and proven leadership of a national organization with the regional insights, longstanding community connections and agility of empowered local teams. The company is one of the 2026 Fortune World’s Most Admired Companies, 2026 Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For®, and recognized as a PEOPLE Companies That Care® (2023-2025) organization. The company was also named as a Great Place To Work-Certified™ company for five years in a row and named on several Great Place To Work® Best Workplaces lists. Tri Pointe has also won multiple Builder of the Year and Developer of the Year awards. Tri Pointe Homes is an award-winning leader in the Bay Area real estate sector. For more information, please visit TriPointeHomes.com.

title: M/I Homes (MHO) Lags Q1 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
content:
M/I Homes (MHO) came out with quarterly earnings of $2.55 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.64 per share. This compares to earnings of $3.98 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of -3.23%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this homebuilder would post earnings of $3.88 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.91, delivering a surprise of +0.77%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates just once.

M/I Homes, which belongs to the Zacks Building Products - Home Builders industry, posted revenues of $920.71 million for the quarter ended March 2026, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.96%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $976.09 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates just once over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

M/I Homes shares have added about 0.7% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 3.2%.

What's Next for M/I Homes?

While M/I Homes has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for M/I Homes was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $3.86 on $1.24 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $13.63 on $4.48 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Building Products - Home Builders is currently in the bottom 10% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the same industry, Tri Pointe Homes (TPH), has yet to report results for the quarter ended March 2026.

This home builder is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.30 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -57.1%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

Tri Pointe Homes' revenues are expected to be $622.7 million, down 13.6% from the year-ago quarter.

title: Final Community Now Selling in Snoqualmie Ridge, Marking the Closing Chapter of a Landmark Eastside Community
content:
Last chance for homebuyers to purchase a brand-new home in one of the Greater Seattle region’s most sought-after neighborhoods

SNOQUALMIE, Wash., April 09, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The final community at Snoqualmie Ridge, one of the Eastside’s largest and most influential planned communities, is now selling. This marks the end of a multi-decade buildout that has helped define residential growth in the Snoqualmie Valley.

Tri Pointe Homes® has opened Timber Trails, a 46-home neighborhood that represents the last subdivision within the more than 1,300-acre Snoqualmie Ridge community. Development on "the Ridge" began in the late 1990s, and over more than two decades the community has grown into a vibrant mix of neighborhoods, retail, schools and recreation.

"This is a rare moment where a community of this scale is truly coming full circle," said Tricia Lynn, vice president of community experience for Tri Pointe Washington. "Snoqualmie Ridge has been shaping how people live on the Eastside for more than 20 years, and Timber Trails represents the final opportunity to be a part of that legacy."

Formerly known as Quadrant Homes®, Tri Pointe Homes Washington has been deeply involved in Snoqualmie Ridge since its earliest phases, helping to plan and build the community and delivering hundreds of homes there over time. The company has operated in the Pacific Northwest since 1969 and has played a leading role in some of the region’s most significant planned communities, including Redmond Ridge and Northwest Landing. It recently celebrated reaching 20,000 homes sold in Washington state.

Snoqualmie Ridge today is widely recognized for its integration of housing, open space and recreation, with miles of trails, parks and preserved natural areas, as well as direct access to Interstate 90 connecting residents to major employment centers in Bellevue and Seattle. The community’s long-term planning approach, combining residential, retail and civic uses, has made it a model for Eastside growth.

The release of Timber Trails comes as opportunities for large-scale planned developments on the Eastside have become increasingly scarce, underscoring the significance of this final phase. For buyers, it represents one of the last chances to purchase a newly built home within a fully established community of this scale and maturity.

Homes at Timber Trails, located at 34314 SE Summit Street, Snoqualmie, WA 98065, feature four distinct floor plans with thoughtfully designed layouts across three-story townhomes and paired homes, or duplexes. Each home offers open-concept main living areas with great rooms, dining areas, and kitchens that connect seamlessly to covered outdoor living. Floor plans range from three to four bedrooms, approximately 3.5 baths, and about 1,900 to 3,100 square feet, with two- to three-bay garages. Homes are anticipated from the low $1 millions.

The company builds premium homes and communities with deep ties to the communities it serves—some for as long as a century. Tri Pointe Homes combines the financial resources, technology platforms and proven leadership of a national organization with the regional insights, longstanding community connections, and agility of empowered local teams. title: Investor Sells Entire Tri Pointe Homes Stake Amid 55% Stock Surge and Pending Deal
content:
O'Keefe Stevens Advisory, Inc. fully exited its position in Tri Pointe Homes(NYSE:TPH), according to an SEC filing dated April 7, 2026, selling 430,731 shares for an estimated $17.52 million based on quarterly average pricing.

What happened

According to an SEC filing dated April 7, 2026, O'Keefe Stevens Advisory, Inc. sold its entire holding of 430,731 shares in Tri Pointe Homes. The estimated transaction value was $17.52 million based on the average closing price for the quarter. This brings the fund’s post-trade position in Tri Pointe Homes to zero shares, eliminating its exposure to the stock.

What else to know

This was a complete exit. Top holdings after the filing:

NASDAQ: NVDA: $63.57 million (15.7% of AUM) NYSE: HCC: $27.26 million (6.7% of AUM) NYSE: GLW: $24.36 million (6.0% of AUM) NYSE: AER: $20.14 million (5.0% of AUM) NYSE: SPHR: $19.81 million (4.9% of AUM) As of April 6, 2026, Tri Pointe Homes shares were priced at $46.79, up 54.9% over the past year and outperforming the S&P 500 by 30.09 percentage points

Company Overview

Metric Value Revenue (TTM) $3.47 billion Net Income (TTM) $241.08 million Price (as of market close 2026-04-06) $46.79 One-Year Price Change 54.88%

Company Snapshot

Tri Pointe Homes, Inc. designs, constructs, and sells single-family attached and detached homes across the United States, operating under six regional brands. The company generates revenue primarily through home sales and also offers mortgage financing, title and escrow, and property and casualty insurance services. Its primary customers are individual homebuyers in various U.S. markets.

What this transaction means for investors

With Tri Pointe shares up nearly 55% over the past year and a pending acquisition in play, this move looks more like locking in gains amid a defined catalyst window than a view on deteriorating fundamentals.

That context matters because Tri Pointe’s underlying business has been mixed even as the stock rallied. Full-year revenue declined to $3.4 billion from $4.4 billion, while net income fell to $241 million from $458 million. Orders and deliveries were also down double digits, and backlog value dropped 42% year over year, pointing to softer forward demand. Meanwhile, margins compressed as well, with homebuilding gross margin falling to 21.0% from 23.3%. This all comes as the announced acquisition by Sumitomo Forestry introduces a ceiling on near-term upside, effectively shifting the stock from a growth story to a merger-arbitrage trade.

Ultimately, the exit likely reflects positioning around a catalyst and not necessarily a judgment on long-term viability. The bigger question is whether housing demand and margins stabilize post-cycle, especially if the deal closes and resets valuation expectations.
